correctness.rationale: A one-parameter diagonal action separates all binary monomials, so fixed points in the product are monomial pairs. For indices i,j their gcd degree is min(i,j)+min(m-i,n-j). With m<=n, the threshold deg gcd>=k becomes the exact diagonal strip k-m<=j-i<=n-k. The two excluded corners each contain k(k+1)/2 lattice points, giving the cumulative formula. Euler localization is valid for the possibly singular projective loci and yields the topological Euler characteristic. Constructible additivity then gives the exact-stratum formulas. The checker independently enumerates exponent pairs and all threshold histograms over a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: The resultant and subresultant loci are among the most classical degeneracy varieties in elimination theory. The theorem gives a complete closed Euler profile for every common-factor threshold and, more finely, every exact gcd-degree stratum. The degree-independent value 2 for coprime projective pairs and the universal linear staircase for positive gcd degree are structural constraints on the entire filtration, not arbitrary numerical slices.
